name: CISO write gate is not diff-aware and gives no location: a comment-only fix of its own finding can never be written
description:
## Defect (found on card 675c4695, shift 3)

`project_write_file` refuses a whole-file write with:

```
Write blocked by CISO: block | high | 1 finding(s) | injection. Rules: injection.hidden-html-comment
```

even when the write **removes** the flagged comment.

### Evidence (reproducible)

Target: `client/src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue` (631 lines, +123/-0 vs HEAD). Three variants were written, differing only in the flagged block at lines 183-185:

1. neutral, non-imperative prose;
2. a label-only marker `<!-- ── Repeat (recurrence) ── -->`, same kind as the `── Identity ──` / `── Assistant ──` markers already in the file;
3. the comment **deleted** (net -3 lines).

All three returned the identical `Write blocked by CISO: block | high | 1 finding(s) | injection`. `project_changes` afterwards still reports `+123/-0`, i.e. nothing was written and the block is not a partial-write artefact.

### Why this is a gate defect and not a finding

- The verdict is computed over the **whole file content**, not over the diff: removing the only flagged comment does not clear it. `security_review_changes` (diff-based) reported exactly 1 finding at `:183`, which the write gate contradicts.
- The error carries **no path:line and no snippet**, so the operator cannot tell which comment triggered it. The remaining candidates are the `<template>` comments inside the `+123` diff, most plausibly `:160-162` (`wake_at` is the alarm clock of the autonomy worker...).
- Net effect: any `.vue` that contains a hidden HTML comment the scanner dislikes becomes **unmodifiable through the write path**, including the edit that would fix it. That is a deadlock: the gate blocks its own remediation.

### Expected behaviour

1. Blame the offending `path:line` in the error (and the snippet), like `security_review_changes` does.
2. Evaluate the change being introduced, not the pre-existing content: a write that deletes or rewords the flagged comment must pass.
3. If the whole-content scan is intentional, expose a documented, audited way to write a remediation (e.g. an explicit acknowledgement argument recording who accepted what), instead of an unconditional refusal.

### Notes

- Distinct from `3a86fba9` (no patch-granularity write). A patch tool would not help here: the gate refuses the write itself, at any granularity.
- The fix lives in the platform backend (CISO guard around the file-write tool), which is outside this project's tool root (`.../codx-junior-platform/client`) - same limitation already recorded on `8a554fa4`. Whoever takes it needs a tool root at the repository root.
- Until it is fixed, card `675c4695` stays open in Working with its acceptance unmet.

### Acceptance

- A write that removes/rewords the flagged comment in `TaskSettings.vue` succeeds and `project_changes` shows a hunk limited to lines 183-185.
- A write that still contains an offending comment fails with `path:line` + snippet in the message.

## Measurement added (shift 3, from card 675c4695)

The failure mode is worse than "not diff-aware", so the diagnosis can be pinned down:

`TaskSettings.vue` holds **11 HTML comment blocks** (6-13, 16, 44, 90, 135-137, 183-185, 250, 255, 307-309, 329). Three observed writes:

| variant of 183-185 | result |
|---|---|
| neutral, non-imperative prose | `block`, **1 finding**, no location |
| label-only marker | `block`, **1 finding**, no location |
| comment **deleted** entirely | `block`, **1 finding**, no location |

Deleting the flagged block still leaves 1 finding, so **at least one other HTML comment also matches `injection.hidden-html-comment`** and the reported finding is not necessarily the one the user/agent set out to fix. Without `path:line` + snippet the operator cannot tell which one it is; with a whole-file-only writer the only "fix" available is a blind rewrite of all comments in a 631-line SFC, which risks dropping code.

### Requested behaviour (unchanged, now with a test)
- Every finding carries `path`, `line` and a 1-line snippet.
- The verdict is computed on the **diff** being written/committed, so a write that removes or neutralises the offending comment passes.
- When several comments match, report **all** of them (count ≥ 2 on this file), not a deduplicated count of 1 per rule.

### Reproduction case
Any write to `client/src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue` from this project (root `.../codx-junior-platform/client`), vendor-free, no behaviour change intended.

## Shift 4 increment — the missing `path:line` localized, and why the gate's finding count proves nothing

**Changed files: none.** This card is a defect of the platform *write path* (the CISO guard around `project_write_file`), which lives outside this project's tool root. Re-verified this shift instead of assumed:

- `project_read_file("../api/pyproject.toml")` → `Path must belong to …/codx-junior-platform/client or to a linked project (read_project_dependencies …)`
- `read_folder("/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform")` → `Invalid path parameter: Path … is not within project root '…/client'`
- `project_read_file("/…/codx-junior-platform/api/pyproject.toml")` → `File not found`

So the guard cannot be read, patched or unit-tested from here. What *is* measurable from here is its input — which is exactly what the gate refuses to report.

### 1. Complete candidate set in the target file (the data the error omits)

`project_read_file("src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue", pattern="<!--")` → **10 hidden HTML comment blocks, all still on disk**:

| lines | kind | in the current diff? |
|---|---|---|
| 6-13 | prose: "── Properties dialog ── The fields of a chat/task, grouped in the three decisions the user actually makes…" | pre-existing |
| 16, 44, 90, 250, 255, 329 | one-line label markers (`── Identity ──`, `Header …`, `Footer …`) | pre-existing |
| **135-137** | **prose, same class as the finding: "`wake_at` is the alarm clock of the autonomy worker, not a deadline … Setting it moves the task to the after-hours shift and draws it in the calendar."** | **pre-existing** |
| **183-185** | **the reported one: "… `wake_at` is armed to the next occurrence; the autonomy runtime re-arms it after every run."** | **added (+123)** |
| 307-309 | prose: "── Danger zone … the destructive action is visible, but a single misclick cannot delete the conversation." | pre-existing |

`project_changes(scope="all", paths=["src/components/kanban/TaskSettings.vue"], include_patch=true)` → still `+123/-0`, three hunks (`@@ -180,4 +180,68 @@`, `@@ -321,4 +385,15 @@`, `@@ -503,4 +578,52 @@`). Nothing has been written since the three blocked variants, so the file state is unchanged and `:183` is an added line.

### 2. Why the card's "≥2 comments match" inference needs restating

- The **diff-based** review could only ever report `:183`: the first hunk starts at line 180, so `:135-137` is outside every hunk. A review count of 1 says nothing about how many matches exist in the *file*.
- The **write gate** scans the file content, so at `:135-137` it sees a block of the same class as the one it flags. Either it matches it (→ count should be ≥2) or it evaluated the **on-disk** content and never looked at the proposed one (→ 1 is the pre-existing `:183`). Both are consistent with `1 finding(s)`; nothing in the current evidence chooses between them.
- Class is set by the rule name and confirmed by content: the same sentences exist as `//` comments at `src/api/modules/chats.js:87-89` ("…the autonomy runtime re-arms it after every run…") and `injection.hidden-html-comment` does not cover JS comments. The trigger is *being hidden in the template*, not being addressed at the agent.

Consequence for `675c4695`: rewording **only** `:183-185` will very likely still be refused — which is what all three blocked variants observed. A remediation write must neutralise every prose block (6-13, 135-137, 183-185, 307-309), i.e. ~14 comment lines, and it must not be attempted by retyping 631 lines (see `3a86fba9`).

### 3. Acceptance refined for whoever owns the guard (needs a repo-root tool root)

1. Error carries `path:line` + one-line snippet for **each** match — no `1 finding(s)` aggregate. Without this the two hypotheses above stay indistinguishable, so this is a prerequisite, not a nicety.
2. Verdict computed on the **proposed content**: a proposed `TaskSettings.vue` with 6-13 / 135-137 / 183-185 / 307-309 neutralised must return `allow`; the unchanged file must still `block`.
3. Scanner-level regression test (no repo needed): (a) current template with only `:183` removed → the report must list the remaining matches individually (this is the test that proves whether the count is deduplicated); (b) all four prose blocks removed → `0 findings`.
4. `3a86fba9` does **not** unblock this: the refusal happens at whole-content scan, at any write granularity. The two fixes are independent.

**Validation evidence available this shift: none executable.** This runtime has no shell and no node (`91411767`, `3a86fba9`), so no test command can be run; every statement above is a tool output (paths, line numbers, unchanged diff) reproduced here. No file was modified by this increment.

Moving to **Review** — status stays `doing`, I do not close my own cards.
